title: 2001 AMC 12 Problem 12
statement: How many positive integers not exceeding \(2001\) are multiples of \(3\) or \(4\) but not \(5?\)

solutions.text:
Multiples of \(3\) or \(4\) up to \(2001\) number \[ 667 + 500 - 166 = 1001, \] using \(\lfloor \frac{2001}{3} \rfloor = 667,\) \(\lfloor \frac{2001}{4} \rfloor = 500,\) and \(\lfloor \frac{2001}{12} \rfloor = 166.\)

Among these, the ones divisible by \(5\) are multiples of \(15\) or \(20\): \[ 133 + 100 - 33 = 200, \] using \(\lfloor \frac{2001}{15} \rfloor = 133,\) \(\lfloor \frac{2001}{20} \rfloor = 100,\) and \(\lfloor \frac{2001}{60} \rfloor = 33.\)

The count is \(1001 - 200 = 801.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: First count multiples of \(3\) or \(4\) using \(\lfloor \frac{2001}{3} \rfloor\) \(+ \lfloor \frac{2001}{4} \rfloor\) \(- \lfloor \frac{2001}{12} \rfloor\)
Then subtract those also divisible by \(5,\) i.e. the multiples of \(15\) or \(20\)
